title: The Lord Is on His Holy Throne
description: The Lord Is on His Holy Throne in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: Lydia Sigourney wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 1005 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “True Prayer”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: The Lord is on his ho-ly throne, He sits in king-ly state; Let those who for his fa-vors seek, In hum-ble si-lence wait.

lines: The Lord is on his holy throne,
Let those who for his favors seek,
True prayer is not th' imposing sound
But the deep silence of a soul

licence: Public domain: Lydia Sigourney died in 1865.
credits: Words by Lydia Sigourney (1791–1865), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
